title: A generating connected-subgroup family has a finite dominant word
statement:
Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field], and let $G$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], geometrically connected [def-weil-connected-scheme, def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], affine $k$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $I$ be a nonempty set and $(H_i\hookrightarrow G)_{i\in I}$ a family of smooth geometrically connected closed $k$-subgroup schemes [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Assume that for every closed $k$-subgroup scheme $K\subseteq G$, containment $H_i\subseteq K$ for all $i\in I$ implies $K=G$. Then there are an integer $n\geq1$ and indices $i_1,\ldots,i_n\in I$, with repetitions allowed, such that the multiplication morphism
$$H_{i_1}\times_k\cdots\times_k H_{i_n}\longrightarrow G,\qquad(h_1,\ldots,h_n)\longmapsto h_1\cdots h_n$$
has dense image in the underlying Zariski topological space of $G$. Products are scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. The set $I$ need not be finite, the subgroups need not be normal or commute, and no infinitude or perfectness assumption is made on $k$.

source.place: Agent-formulated general finite-word prerequisite implicit in the proof of Corollary 17.92, printed p.382; compare section 2h, Propositions 2.50-2.53, printed pp.55-56, on generated smooth connected subgroups. The maximal-dimension word-closure argument is supplied by the worker, not claimed to be stated verbatim by Milne.

proof.text: For each nonempty finite word $v=(j_1,\ldots,j_r)$ in $I$, put $P_v=H_{j_1}\times_k\cdots\times_kH_{j_r}$ and let $w_v:P_v\to G$ multiply its factors in that order. By [def-weil-closed-immersion], each $H_i$ is affine, with coordinate algebra a quotient of $A=k[G]$, hence finitely generated over $k$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Repeatedly applying [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] gives $P_v=\operatorname{Spec}B_v$, where $B_v$ is the corresponding finite tensor product of the coordinate algebras. Its finite tensor factors have finite generating sets, whose images together generate $B_v$, so $P_v$ has finite type. Since each $H_i$ is affine and smooth over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] makes $k\to k[H_i]$ a smooth ring map; base change followed by composition in [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-base-change-composition] makes $k\to B_v$ smooth, and [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map-iff-smooth-affine] again shows that $P_v$ is smooth over $k$. It has the $k$-point $o_v$ with all coordinates the identity [def-sc-group-scheme, def-pc-fibre-product]. Induct on $r$ to see that $P_v$ is connected: the one-letter case is a hypothesis, and [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-product-components] applied to $H_{j_1}$ and the remaining product gives exactly one connected component at each induction step. Its geometric-connectedness hypothesis is the given hypothesis on $H_{j_1}$; the remaining product is nonempty because of $o_v$.

source.place: Agent-supplied maximal-dimension word argument for Corollary 17.92, printed p.382, using the affine generated-subgroup construction of Proposition 2.46, printed pp.54–55.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular] to $P_v\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. In particular all local rings at closed points are regular. Thus [lem-wf-smooth-components-disjoint], with its affine and finite-type hypotheses supplied by step 1, identifies its irreducible components with its connected components. Since $P_v$ is nonempty and connected, it is irreducible. Its coordinate algebra $B_v$ is smooth over the field $k$ by step 1, so [lem-sc-smooth-algebra-reduced-field] makes it reduced. Consequently $P_v$ is integral and $B_v$ is an integral domain by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. This conclusion holds for every nonempty word, including words with repeated indices.

source.place: Agent-supplied maximal-dimension word argument for Corollary 17.92, printed p.382, using the affine generated-subgroup construction of Proposition 2.46, printed pp.54–55.

proof.text: Let $J_v=\ker(w_v^*:A\to B_v)$ and $Z_v=\operatorname{Spec}(A/J_v)\subseteq G$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient, def-weil-closed-immersion]. The ideal $J_v$ is prime: its quotient embeds in the nonzero domain $B_v$. The point $(0)\in\operatorname{Spec}B_v$ maps to $J_v\in\operatorname{Spec}A$, and every point in the image of $w_v$ contains $J_v$. The closure formula in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes] therefore shows $\overline{w_v(|P_v|)}=V(J_v)=|Z_v|$, and that this set is nonempty and irreducible. By [lem-kun-dimension-finite-type], the Krull dimension of $G$ is a finite integer $D$. With dimension defined by [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], every chain in the closed subspace $Z_v$ is a chain in $G$, so $0\leq\dim Z_v\leq D$. The words form a nonempty set, since $I$ is nonempty. Choose a word $v$ for which $d=\dim Z_v$ is maximal, and fix $J=J_v$ and $Z=Z_v$.

source.place: Agent-supplied maximal-dimension word argument for Corollary 17.92, printed p.382, using the affine generated-subgroup construction of Proposition 2.46, printed pp.54–55.

proof.text: For any nonempty word $u$, inserting identity elements gives morphisms $P_v\to P_{vu}$ and $P_u\to P_{vu}$ whose composites with $w_{vu}$ are $w_v$ and $w_u$ [def-sc-group-scheme, def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus $Z_v\subseteq Z_{vu}$ and $Z_u\subseteq Z_{vu}$ on underlying spaces. If the first inclusion were proper, a chain of length $d$ in $Z_v$, followed by the irreducible closed set $Z_{vu}$, would be a chain of length $d+1$ in $Z_{vu}$, contradicting maximality. Such a length-$d$ chain exists because the finite integer $d$ is the supremum in [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Hence $|Z_{vu}|=|Z|$, and the uniqueness and inclusion assertions for prime ideals in [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-closed-subsets-primes] give $J_{vu}=J$ and $J\subseteq J_u$. In particular every word image lies in $Z$. More generally any word $t$ containing $v$ as a consecutive block has $Z_v\subseteq Z_t$ by the same identity insertion, hence $J_t=J$ by the identical chain argument.

source.place: Agent-supplied maximal-dimension word argument for Corollary 17.92, printed p.382, using the affine generated-subgroup construction of Proposition 2.46, printed pp.54–55.

proof.text: Put $X=P_v\times_kP_v$, $o=(o_v,o_v)$, and $\varphi(x,y)=w_v(x)w_v(y)^{-1}$, using the group morphisms and products of [def-sc-group-scheme, def-pc-fibre-product]. This is a $k$-morphism, $\varphi(o)=e$, and for every commutative $k$-algebra $R$ the image $\varphi(X(R))$ is inverse-stable: $\varphi(x,y)^{-1}=\varphi(y,x)$. If $v^{\mathrm{rev}}$ is the word with its indices reversed, the map $(y_1,\ldots,y_r)\mapsto(y_r^{-1},\ldots,y_1^{-1})$ is an isomorphism $P_v\to P_{v^{\mathrm{rev}}}$, its inverse given by the same reversal and inverses. Under this coordinate isomorphism, $\varphi$ is the word map for $vv^{\mathrm{rev}}$. For each $n\geq1$, the map $X^n\to G$ multiplying $n$ values of $\varphi$ is therefore the word map for $(vv^{\mathrm{rev}})^n$, precomposed with the product of those isomorphisms. This word contains the block $v$, so step 4 gives its kernel $J$; precomposition with an isomorphism preserves that kernel.

source.place: Agent-supplied maximal-dimension word argument for Corollary 17.92, printed p.382, using the affine generated-subgroup construction of Proposition 2.46, printed pp.54–55.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-pointed-map-generated-subgroup] to $X,o,\varphi$. The ambient $G$ is affine of finite type over the field $k$. The scheme $X$ is affine of finite type by step 1, applied to the word $vv$; step 5 supplies the rational point, the identity condition, and inverse-stability for every $k$-algebra. The cited statement constructs a closed subgroup $L=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\bigcap_{n\geq1}\ker((\varphi^n)^*))$. Every kernel in this nonempty intersection is $J$ by step 5, so $L=\operatorname{Spec}(A/J)=Z$ as closed subschemes of $G$. Thus $Z$ is a closed $k$-subgroup scheme, not just a closed set stable on $k$-rational points.

source.place: Agent-supplied maximal-dimension word argument for Corollary 17.92, printed p.382, using the affine generated-subgroup construction of Proposition 2.46, printed pp.54–55.

proof.text: For a one-letter word $(i)$, step 4 gives $J\subseteq J_{(i)}=\ker(A\to k[H_i])$. Hence $a+J\mapsto w_{(i)}^*(a)$ is a well-defined $k$-algebra map $A/J\to k[H_i]$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]. Its spectrum is the factorization $H_i\to Z\to G$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. This says $H_i\subseteq Z$ as closed subgroup schemes [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. The generation hypothesis of the item, applied to the closed subgroup $Z$ from step 6, forces $Z=G$. Step 3 now gives $\overline{w_v(|P_v|)}=|G|$. The chosen word was nonempty, so its length is the required $n\geq1$, and its entries supply the required indices.
